workflow_pattern: This is a 'F6_mcp_heavy' style workflow. It requires the following operations, in roughly this order: create repository, init multiple branches, add readme with content, propagate and enhance readme across branches, create directory structure with init files, create workflow conditional comment by label, validate automation with test issues. The task should combine these operations into one coherent, realistic request without listing them as separate steps.
question:
Hi there! I'm a team lead setting up an LLM eval harness and need help setting up a new project repository called EvalHarness-Core, which will support the development of an evaluation harness leveraging the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for assessing LLM capabilities. Please create the repository with two branches: main and dev. The main branch should contain a README.md file with the following content: "# EvalHarness-Core
A comprehensive evaluation harness for benchmarking LLMs using the Model Context Protocol." The dev branch should also start with the same README.md content but with an additional reference link to the official MCP GitHub repository to help collaborators understand the underlying technology. In the dev branch, please set up the project structure with three directories: core, adapters, and reporters, each containing an __init__.py file with a simple comment: "# This is a test comment". Additionally, I'd like to include a GitHub automation script that listens for newly created issues and posts an automatic comment based on the assigned label: for issues labeled bug, comment "Thank you. We will fix it."; for issues labeled feature, comment "Thank you, we will consider to include this feature."; and for issues labeled discussion, comment "Thanks for starting this discussion! We welcome community input." Please create sample issues titled "Adapter crashes on empty response" (with label bug), "Feature: pluggable reporter backends" (with label feature), and "Discussion: scoring rubric alignment" (with label discussion) with appropriate labels to test the automation. Thank you so much for your assistance!
